themes.consensus_view: Desks agree the Treasury is buying back long-dated bonds to hold down long-term borrowing costs, but they split on whether that changes where yields end up or just shifts the pressure onto a weaker dollar.

facts_agreed.claim: The Treasury is actively using long-end buybacks to manage how much long-dated debt the market has to hold.
evidence_quotes: The Treasury is showing a strong preference to subdue term premium.
The response to pressure in the long end can include changing the way Treasury manages duration.
US Treasury liquidity support buyback operations

facts_agreed.claim: Supporting long-dated bond prices carries a cost that shows up in the dollar.
evidence_quotes: Supporting bonds may come at the expense of letting the USD become the adjustment valve.

facts_contested.claim: whether buybacks change where long-end yields ultimately settle
facts_contested.for_evidence: The bull flattener makes sense in this context.
facts_contested.against_evidence: Twists can change the path, but they rarely change the destination.

themes.consensus_view: Three banks mention US pressure on Iran as background risk in this window, but none of them takes a side on where it goes or what it does to markets.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag US-Iran pressure and sanctions as a live background risk this window without staking a directional view.

themes.consensus_view: Three desks flag the falling cost of running AI models as a live subject this window, but none of them has staked out a directional call on what it does to prices.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks reference the declining cost of running AI models as an ongoing development worth tracking.

themes.consensus_view: Both banks with a view here say AI spending is still growing and is now better covered by real revenue, with Goldman calling for $1-1.5 trillion of spending next year and JPMorgan sizing the 2026-2030 buildout at $5-10 trillion, and nobody in this set arguing the other side.

facts_agreed.claim: The AI spending cycle is still expanding and looks economically justified by the revenue it is generating.
evidence_quotes: recent acceleration in AI companies' revenues makes the AI capex cycle look more economically viable
AI demand/capex is still growing (1-1.5trn for next year)
